title: What you should NOT be doing during a bulk
summary: NH recounts bulking from 120 to 240 lbs over 7-8 years: the 120-190 phase was nearly textbook, but chasing weightlifting strength he overate to 240 lbs at 6 ft and got fat, realizing it only after breaking his ribs squatting. He advises a surplus no bigger than 10-15%, tracking calories or eating instinctively while monitoring the scale, and near-maintenance lean gaining over dirty bulking.

claims.claim: A bulk is a caloric surplus to gain mass; for naturals past puberty that mass is muscle, fat and water, with negligible bone or connective-tissue gain.
You will gain fat on a bulk; the goal is to minimise fat and maximise muscle. Anyone claiming 20 lbs of muscle with no fat is lying.
Excess bulking fat deposits around organs (unhealthy) and the waist (looks bad).
NH started as a very skinny 120 lbs and went to 240 lbs over about 7-8 years.
His bulk from 120 to about 190 lbs was nearly textbook: just enough surplus that he looked bigger, never fatter.
Around 190 lbs he got into weightlifting, ate a ton, strength rose fast, and he gained fat in his lower back and love handles up to 240 lbs.
At 6 ft with a small frame, 240 lbs was far too heavy; breaking both ribs squatting made him realize he was fat, not massive.
There's no muscle-gain benefit to a surplus above 10-15%; beyond that it's fat.
Staying slightly above maintenance throughout your lifting career keeps adding muscle.
A larger surplus improves recovery and heavier bodyweight helps move more weight ('mass moves mass'), but that doesn't matter if you care about aesthetics.
Either count calories precisely to keep the surplus in range, or eat instinctively to fullness while monitoring the scale.
'I can still see my abs' is a trap: he could, through a thick layer of fat.
He believes he would have gained as much muscle and strength with a much smaller surplus.
Fat gained in that period is stubborn and taking forever to lose despite visible veins, a six-pack and cuts elsewhere.
His naturally wide waist makes the leftover fat look less out of place.
Gallon-of-milk dirty bulking is advice only for very skinny people, and even they should mind their health.
Normal people should stay at maintenance or a tiny surplus and gain strength; slower progress gives lean mass.
Bodybuilding is an exercise of patience; accept slower progress if it serves your goals.
